module purpose: neorv32_debug_dtm synchronizes JTAG TCK/TDI/TMS into the clk_i domain, runs a JTAG TAP controller, captures and shifts IDCODE/DTMCS/DMI data on jtag_tdo_o, and turns JTAG DMI updates into internal DMI request state that drives dmi_req_o while latching dmi_rsp_i data for later JTAG readout.

use-case flows.value: synchronized JTAG samples and derived TCK edge/TMS/TDI values used by the TAP logic
TAP controller state sequencing on synchronized TCK and TMS
instruction register contents captured and shifted to select the active data register and TDO source
selected IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI, or bypass register bits shifted on jtag_tdo_o
DTM reset control flags loaded from DTMCS and auto-cleared when not busy
DMI request address, write data, and operation extracted from the DMI register and issued when a DR update selects DMI
DMI response data latched from dmi_rsp_i and exposed through the DMI readout path
sticky DMI error status set or cleared and exposed through DMI/DTMCS readout
asynchronous clearing of TAP, trigger, register, output, and DMI control state while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: tap_ctrl_state advances only on synchronized TCK rising edges (121-139) and then controls DR update generation (151-156), IR capture/shift (178-181), DR capture/shift (185-199), and TDO selection (202-210). Wrong state corrupts these implemented phases, so integrity is established; availability is also established because reset initializes LOGIC_RESET (119) and later synchronized TCK/TMS transitions move the state machine.

tap_reg.ireg is forced to the IDCODE instruction in LOGIC_RESET or IR_CAPTURE (178-179), shifted from TDI in IR_SHIFT (180-181), selects which data register is captured or shifted (186-197), selects the TDO source (203-210), and gates DTMCS/DMI handling in the DMI controller (247,258,265). Integrity is established because register selection and downstream control depend on the exact instruction value; availability is established by the explicit capture, shift, and IR readout behavior.

When DR_CAPTURE selects IDCODE, tap_reg.idcode loads `IDCODE_VERSION & IDCODE_PARTID & IDCODE_MANID & '1'` (185-187); in DR_SHIFT it shifts serially (192-194); and jtag_tdo_o outputs tap_reg.idcode when IDCODE is selected (206-207). The RTL therefore establishes the integrity of the reported identification value; availability is established by the explicit capture and shift path. The generic sources are not candidates, so the listed references are the internal storage and exit points.

conceptual assets.concept: DTM reset control flags in effect (dmireset and dmihardreset)
conceptual assets.reasoning: On a DR update with DTMCS selected, dmi_ctrl.dmireset and dmi_ctrl.dmihardreset take tap_reg.dtmcs bits 16 and 17 (247-249); when not busy they clear (250-252). These flags clear dmi_ctrl.err (256-257), gate DMI request acceptance (265), and are reported back through DTMCS bits 16 and 17 (220-221, 188, 208). Integrity is established because request blocking, error clearing, and reported control state depend on the exact flag values; availability is established by the explicit latch and clear behavior.

dmi_ctrl.busy is asserted when a valid DMI read or write request is accepted (265-270) and is cleared only when `dmi_rsp_i.ack = '1'` in the busy path (273-276). The module uses this state to clear DTM reset flags only when idle (250-252), to raise overlap error on a new DMI update while busy (258-259), to block new request acceptance (264-270), and to select response capture behavior (273-276). Integrity is established because those implemented behaviors depend on whether a transaction is outstanding; availability is established by the explicit set and clear conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: Issued DMI request contents (address, write data, and operation)
conceptual assets.reasoning: When idle and not in dmihardreset, a DR update with DMI selected copies tap_reg.dmi bits 40:34 into dmi_ctrl.addr and bits 33:2 into dmi_ctrl.wdata (265-267); if bits 1:0 encode read or write, dmi_ctrl.op takes that opcode and busy is set (268-270). These internal fields directly drive dmi_req_o (283-285). Because dmi_req_o/dmi_rsp_i together form a request/response transport record, the transport port is excluded; the internal dmi_ctrl fields that store the issued request are the structural assets. Integrity is established because the external consumer must receive the exact request defined by lines 265-269; availability is established under those same explicit acceptance conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI read data returned to the JTAG reader
conceptual assets.reasoning: In the busy path, dmi_ctrl.rdata copies `dmi_rsp_i.data` (274) and is then packed into tap_reg.dmi_nxt together with the address and error bits (229); when DMI is selected in DR_CAPTURE, tap_reg.dmi takes that packaged value (185, 189), and jtag_tdo_o shifts tap_reg.dmi when DMI is selected (206, 209). Because dmi_rsp_i is the response side of the transport record, it is excluded; the internal capture points and the JTAG exit are reported instead. Integrity is established because the JTAG reader must receive the exact returned data defined by these lines; availability is established when a response is captured and later selected for DR capture and shift.

dmi_ctrl.err clears when dmireset or dmihardreset is asserted (256-257) and sets when a new DMI update arrives while busy and DMI is selected (258-259). The status is packed into tap_reg.dmi_nxt by `replicate_f(dmi_ctrl.err, 2)` (229) and mirrored into DTMCS bits 11:10 through tap_reg.dmi_nxt(1 downto 0) (224), so it can be captured into DMI or DTMCS (188-189) and shifted on TDO (208-209). Integrity is established because reported fault status must match the implemented overlap and reset conditions; availability is established because the flag is latched until explicit reset and exposed through both readout paths.
